source: STEER Project (Save the Children, iDE Cambodia, and the Cambodian Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries) - "Guide on Banana Cultivation Techniques" (សៀវភៅណែនាំស្តីអំពី បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះដំណាំចេក), February 2020
text:
Black Sigatoka is a fungal leaf disease that produces streak-like lesions on the leaf, 1-2 millimeters wide, which enlarge and darken toward the leaf tip over time, eventually reducing the plant's functional leaf area and, in severe cases, weakening bunch fill. Management includes removing and destroying infected leaves, avoiding overly dense planting that traps humidity, ensuring good field sanitation, and applying a registered fungicide such as mancozeb or copper oxychloride.

A related disease, Cercospora leaf spot (caused by Cercospora musae, sometimes called yellow Sigatoka), produces oval spots with dark borders and a pale center scattered across the leaf; in advanced infection, spots merge into larger dead patches that can kill the leaf outright. It spreads especially in humid conditions and is managed with sanitation and a copper-based fungicide such as copper hydroxide, applied to protect new growth.
